text.p: Standard Financial Inc said Tuesday it has filed a federal lawsuit alleging that LaSalle/Kross Partners LP, which owns 5.4 percent of the thrift, violated federal securities law.

The suit charges that the investment fund falsely stated in an SEC filing that it had acquired its stake in Standard Financial for investment purposes, Standard Financial general counsel Randall Schwartz said in a telephone interview.
Schwartz said LaSalle/Kross has a history of acquiring stakes in thrifts to put them into play as takeover targets.
LaSalle/Kross officials were not available for comment Tuesday.

The lawsuit, filed in Chicago, seeks a temporary restraining order keeping LaSalle/Kross, for a period of 30 days, from acquiring additional Standard Financial shares, selling any of its existing shares, voting any of the shares, or attempting to control or influence Standard Financial's affairs.

LaSalle/Kross said Monday it planned to nominate two people for election to Standard Financial's board of directors. Standard Financial last month changed its bylaws to require 120 days' advance notice on nominations to the board of directors.
